solutionSource.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

entries.clue: Source of information to frustrate directors (9)

blocks.note: to dash hopes is to frustrate them
a company's directors sit on its board

annotation.surface: Someone feeding a company's directors misleading figures to thwart them.
annotation.walkthrough: The surface reads as office politics; the definition is the panel of dials in a car, or its screen equivalent on a computer.
annotation.definitionFit: Its dials show speed, fuel and warnings at a glance, so a car's dashboard is a source of information by function.

entries.clue: Escape? Run away from soldier in attack taking wrong direction (9)

indicatorNotes.Run away from: R (run) goes away from the word for soldier
indicatorNotes.in: the shortened soldier sits in the word for attack
indicatorNotes.taking wrong direction: the attack word is written the wrong way round

blocks.note: a sapper is a military engineer
R is the cricket abbreviation for run

annotation.surface: A soldier fleeing mid-attack after heading the wrong way.
annotation.walkthrough: SAPPER loses its R and the remainder goes inside the reversed attack. The question mark flags that disappearing is only one kind of escape.
annotation.definitionFit: Definition by example: vanishing from sight is one way to escape.

entries.clue: European bridge framed in modest beam (11)

indicatorNotes.framed in: the first pieces are surrounded by the word for modest, as a picture by its frame

blocks.note: an arch spans a gap, as a bridge does

annotation.surface: A modest wooden beam holding up a European bridge.
annotation.walkthrough: The surface makes beam a piece of timber in a bridge; here it is a beam of light.
annotation.definitionFit: The lamp stands for what it throws: a searchlight is named by the beam it casts across the sky.

entries.clue: Sailor picked up the reader in Louisiana creek (5)

indicatorNotes.picked up: in a down clue, lifting the sailor word reads it bottom to top

blocks.note: the person reading the clue is you

annotation.surface: A sailor in Louisiana collecting someone who reads.
annotation.walkthrough: The surface has the sailor collecting a passenger; picked up only turns AB over in this down entry.
annotation.definitionFit: A regional word: bayou is the Louisiana name, from the Choctaw, for a slow marshy creek off the Mississippi.

entries.clue: Weak, lacking power to sustain line of muscular development? (8)

indicatorNotes.lacking: the word for weak goes without P
indicatorNotes.to sustain: what is left holds up, and so contains, L

blocks.note: a pathetic effort is a weak one

annotation.surface: A feeble program that cannot keep up a course of body-building.
annotation.walkthrough: Weak and athletic are opposites, which is the joke: take P out of the feeble word and the strong one appears.
annotation.definitionFit: Said of a build, athletic describes a well-muscled body, so 'of muscular development' is a descriptive paraphrase.

entries.clue: Refusal to accept trade involving province (6)

indicatorNotes.involving: the trade word takes in the province

blocks.note: NI = Northern Ireland, often called the Province

annotation.surface: Someone rejecting a trade agreement that affects a province.
annotation.walkthrough: Northern Ireland is referred to in Britain as 'the Province', hence NI.
annotation.definitionFit: Plain synonym, and also the psychological sense: being in denial is refusing to accept a painful truth.

entries.clue: One keen to follow skipper or admiral? (13)

annotation.definition: One keen to follow skipper or admiral?

blocks.note: the surface suggests a loyal crewman; the setter means an enthusiast who tracks and studies
not ship's officers but butterflies: the skippers are a butterfly family and the red admiral a common species

annotation.surface: An eager sailor wanting to serve under a ship's captain or an admiral.
annotation.walkthrough: Skipper and admiral look naval, but both are butterflies, so the follower is a butterfly enthusiast.
annotation.definitionFit: A lepidopterist studies butterflies and moths, so chasing skippers and red admirals is the job.

entries.clue: Archaic forgotten activity one observed in Victorian novel (5,5)

blocks.note: lorn is an old word for forsaken or forgotten

annotation.surface: An outdated pastime someone spotted in a nineteenth-century novel.
annotation.walkthrough: Archaic is part of the wordplay, labelling lorn as an old word, not describing the novel.
annotation.definitionFit: Definition by example: R. D. Blackmore's Exmoor romance appeared in 1869, in Queen Victoria's reign.

entries.clue: What groundsman will strive to do, picking up note ideally? (7,5)

annotation.definition: What groundsman will strive to do

blocks.clueFragment: What groundsman will strive to do
blocks.note: a groundsman tends the cricket or football pitch and wants to perfect it
the gift of recognising any musical note heard

annotation.surface: A groundsman, whose aim is noted to be ideal.
annotation.walkthrough: The first reading is a verb phrase, perfect the pitch; the second is a noun for a musician's ear. Picking up means hearing, not lifting.
annotation.definitionFit: Perfect used as a verb gives the groundsman's aim; as an adjective, the ideal musical ear.

entries.clue: Tragic situation involving children? It’s no longer current in Athens (7)

annotation.definition: It’s no longer current in Athens

indicatorNotes.involving: the tragic word takes the children inside it

blocks.note: a drama is a tragic or tense situation

annotation.surface: A news item on a sad episode involving children, now out of date in Athens.
annotation.walkthrough: Current is a pun on currency: the drachma was replaced by the euro in 2002.
annotation.definitionFit: Current as in currency: Greece's old coin stopped circulating when the euro arrived.

entries.clue: Style that’s good following some writing on hot atmosphere and economy (7,7)

indicatorNotes.following: to follow is to come after, so the exclamation is placed after the writing

blocks.note: 'Boy!' is an exclamation of delight, as in 'Oh boy!'

annotation.surface: Praise for a piece of prose about climate and the economy.
annotation.walkthrough: Style looks like writing style, which the surface's prose encourages; it means hairstyle.
annotation.definitionFit: Definition by example: a pageboy is a hairstyle, a straight bob with the ends turned under.

entries.clue: Letter seen in English stone within large building (7)

indicatorNotes.within: the stone goes inside the building

blocks.note: a pile is a large imposing building
st = stone, the British unit of 14 pounds

annotation.surface: A letter found carved into English stone inside a big building.
annotation.walkthrough: Letter is a missive here, not a character of the alphabet carved in stone.
annotation.definitionFit: Plain synonym, especially for the formal letters of the New Testament such as Paul's epistles.

entries.clue: Extravagant logo for channel linked to form of comedy? (11)

blocks.note: an ident is a TV channel's short identifying logo sequence

annotation.surface: A lavish television logo for a comedy channel.
annotation.walkthrough: The pieces read in the reverse of clue order: the comedy comes first, the ident follows.
annotation.definitionFit: Improvident means failing to provide for the future, which is how an extravagant spender behaves.

entries.clue: Competitive player dismissing grand row (4)

indicatorNotes.dismissing: G is sent away from the player

blocks.note: a tiger is a fierce competitor

annotation.surface: A fierce competitor getting rid of a big name in a quarrel.
annotation.walkthrough: Row is a line of seats, not a quarrel.
annotation.definitionFit: Plain synonym in the seating sense: the rising rows of a stadium or wedding cake are its tiers.

entries.clue: Wavering attempt to play host to a King (5)

indicatorNotes.to play host to: the attempt word holds the others as its guests

blocks.note: a shy is a throw or try, as at a coconut shy at a British fair

annotation.surface: A nervous effort at entertaining a visiting king.
annotation.walkthrough: Host looks like the royal visit's host; it only signals that SHY holds the rest.
annotation.definitionFit: Plain synonym: a shaky voice or a shaky commitment is a wavering one.

entries.clue: Special payments on or after end of lavish operatic performance (9)

indicatorNotes.after: ON and OR come after the H
indicatorNotes.end of: take the last letter of lavish

blocks.note: an aria is an operatic solo

annotation.surface: Bonuses paid on the back of a lavish opera production.
annotation.walkthrough: On and or are used as themselves, not as signals.
annotation.definitionFit: Honoraria are voluntary fees paid for services where no fee is formally required.

entries.clue: Look for one returning, clutching signs of leg injury (7)

indicatorNotes.returning: the abbreviation for 'for one' goes back to front
indicatorNotes.clutching: it grips the signs of injury between its letters

annotation.surface: Someone checking whether a returning player shows signs of a leg injury.
annotation.walkthrough: Look is a noun here, not a command to search.
annotation.definitionFit: A glimpse is the briefest kind of look, a sighting caught in passing.

entries.clue: Modest work of art? (8,2,2,10)

blocks.note: the surface wants an adjective, unassuming; the setter means a first name, the composer Modest Mussorgsky
not a painting but a musical work, one that happens to be about paintings

annotation.surface: An unassuming artwork.
annotation.walkthrough: Modest is not an adjective but a name: Modest Mussorgsky, whose piano suite depicts a walk round an exhibition of paintings.
annotation.definitionFit: Mussorgsky's 1874 suite is Modest's work, and its subject is literally works of art.

entries.clue: Peer consumed by own daring (8)

indicatorNotes.consumed by: the peer is swallowed up by the word for own

blocks.note: to fess (up) is to own up, admit
an earl is a peer of the realm

annotation.surface: A nobleman eaten up by his own boldness.
annotation.walkthrough: Own is a verb, to admit, and fess is the informal form of confess.
annotation.definitionFit: Plain synonym: someone without fear is bold enough to dare.

entries.clue: Most of shed, knocked over, is … (8)

indicatorNotes.Most of: most, not all, of the word is used, so its last letter goes
indicatorNotes.knocked over: the shortened word is turned over, back to front

annotation.surface: An unfinished sentence about a shed that has been blown over.
annotation.walkthrough: The three dots are the definition: the clue trails off, and that trailing mark is an ellipsis. The dots also lead into 20 across.
annotation.definitionFit: The printed '…' is itself the thing named: those three dots are an ellipsis.

entries.clue: Example sum with variable quantity? Not quite right about that (9)

indicatorNotes.Not quite: drop the last letter of right
indicatorNotes.about: the shortened word goes around the sum and variable

blocks.note: to tot up is to add; a tot is a sum
y is a variable in algebra

annotation.surface: An algebra problem whose answer is almost right.
annotation.walkthrough: The question mark ends the first sentence; 'about that' then wraps the shortened PROPER around everything before it.
annotation.definitionFit: A prototype is the first model that others copy, an example in the sense of a pattern.

entries.clue: … awkward: study flat board around rear of arbour (8)

indicatorNotes.around: the flat board goes around the letter
indicatorNotes.rear of: take the last letter of arbour

blocks.note: a tray is a flat board for carrying things

annotation.surface: Following on from 18: a clumsy woodwork project in a garden bower.
annotation.walkthrough: The leading dots join this to 18 across, whose last word is 'is'; read together, 'Most of shed, knocked over, is awkward'.
annotation.definitionFit: A contrary person deliberately does the opposite, which makes them awkward to deal with.

entries.clue: Best thing scoring one point in Scrabble, looking back (5)

blocks.clueFragment: thing scoring one point in Scrabble
blocks.note: an E tile scores one point in Scrabble

annotation.surface: Reflecting on the best Scrabble move worth just one point.
annotation.walkthrough: Every letter of ELITE is a one-point Scrabble tile, which makes the surface neat.
annotation.definitionFit: The elite is the pick of a group, used adjectivally as in 'elite troops', the best.

entries.clue: Yellow verge featuring in no poetic work (8)

indicatorNotes.featuring in: the verge appears inside the work

blocks.note: prose is writing that is not verse
a rim is an edge, a verge

annotation.surface: A yellow roadside verge, of the kind no poem describes.
annotation.walkthrough: Verge looks like a grassy roadside, which suits yellow flowers; it just means edge.
annotation.definitionFit: A colour named after a flower: primrose is the pale yellow of the spring primrose.

entries.clue: Enclave, perhaps, reflecting term for Lesotho, surrounded by African country (6)

indicatorNotes.reflecting: the whole is mirrored, read backwards
indicatorNotes.term for: term = end, so the last letter of Lesotho
indicatorNotes.surrounded by: that letter sits inside the country

annotation.surface: Lesotho, an enclave surrounded by another African country.
annotation.walkthrough: The surface is true of South Africa, which wholly surrounds Lesotho, so 'African country' begs to be South Africa; it is Niger.
annotation.definitionFit: Definition by example, marked by 'perhaps': an enclave is one kind of region, a territory enclosed by another.

entries.clue: Nearly half British will go round a Francophone country in Asia (6)

indicatorNotes.Nearly half: take just under half of British, its first three letters
indicatorNotes.will go round: those letters surround the French article

annotation.surface: British people circling a French-speaking country in Asia.
annotation.walkthrough: Francophone looks like it describes the country; it only says to put a into French.
annotation.definitionFit: Definition by example: Brunei is a small sultanate on Borneo in South-East Asia.

entries.clue: Sound of engine, European, will enthral a driver (9)

indicatorNotes.will enthral: to enthral is to hold captive, so the pieces hold A inside

annotation.surface: An engine's noise captivating a European motorist.
annotation.walkthrough: The a that seems to belong to 'a driver' is taken into the wordplay.
annotation.definitionFit: A chauffeur is a driver by profession, paid to drive someone else's car.

entries.clue: Surprised comment about new item expected to succeed in virtuoso piece (8)

indicatorNotes.about: the exclamation goes around the other pieces

blocks.note: 'Coo!' is dated British slang for surprise
a cert is a certainty, a horse sure to win

annotation.surface: Someone surprised at a new sure-fire hit in a showpiece.
annotation.walkthrough: Item expected to succeed sounds like a product launch; a cert is racing slang for a sure winner.
annotation.definitionFit: A concerto is written to show off a soloist, making it a virtuoso piece by design.

entries.clue: Absorb article about science in final issue (9)

indicatorNotes.in: that bundle goes inside the final issue

annotation.surface: Taking in a science piece in the last edition of a magazine.
annotation.walkthrough: Article and issue both suggest a magazine; absorb means engross, not soak up.
annotation.definitionFit: Absorb in the sense of engross: what fascinates you holds your whole attention.

entries.clue: Mental activity beginning to tire after all the same disposal of corpses (7,7)

indicatorNotes.beginning to: take the first letter of tire
indicatorNotes.after: that letter follows the word for all the same
indicatorNotes.disposal of: to dispose is also to arrange, so the corpses are set out in a new order

annotation.surface: A mortician's work, draining after the same routine of getting rid of bodies.
annotation.walkthrough: The grim surface hides a cheerful mechanism: disposal is just the signal to rearrange.
annotation.definitionFit: A thought process is the chain of reasoning in the mind, mental activity described step by step.

entries.clue: Ornamental cherub fake? Palace’s final disgrace (3,2,5)

indicatorNotes.final: take the last letter of palace

blocks.note: a putto is a cherub figure in Renaissance and Baroque art

annotation.surface: A scandal over a fake cherub statue in a palace.
annotation.walkthrough: Putto is the Italian word (plural putti) for the chubby winged boys in decorative art.
annotation.definitionFit: An idiom for a verb: to put someone to shame is to disgrace them, often by outshining them.

entries.clue: Pressure over chap’s obsession after ignoring initial scamming (8)

indicatorNotes.over: in a down clue, P sits over (above) the rest
indicatorNotes.after ignoring initial: the obsession word drops its first letter

blocks.note: to have a thing about something is to be obsessed with it

annotation.surface: Pressure on a man because of his fixation with an online fraud.
annotation.walkthrough: Initial looks like a first payment in a scam; it means the first letter of THING.
annotation.definitionFit: Definition by example: phishing is the scam of sending fake messages to steal passwords and bank details.

entries.clue: Small amount of film used in examination (4)

blocks.note: film reels are stored in cans

annotation.surface: A short clip of film shown during an examination.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Small amount' reads as one phrase, but small alone gives S.
annotation.definitionFit: Definition by example: a medical scan is an examination of the body by imaging.

entries.clue: Corruption involving rigged game’s ending and award (7)

indicatorNotes.involving: the corruption word takes the rigged word inside
indicatorNotes.ending: take the last letter of game

annotation.surface: A scandal about a fixed contest and the prize awarded.
annotation.walkthrough: The surface is a match-fixing story; rigged is just SET, as a stage or trap is set.
annotation.definitionFit: Definition by example: a ribbon rosette is the prize given at horse and dog shows.

entries.clue: Bar with nothing in beer, for contrast (12)

indicatorNotes.in: the nought goes inside the beer

blocks.note: the bar in a pub is the counter

annotation.surface: A pub with nothing in its beer, by way of contrast.
annotation.walkthrough: Bar, beer and nothing all stay in the pub for the surface; for is only a link.
annotation.definitionFit: From music to general use: a counterpoint is an element that sets off another by contrast.

entries.clue: Unbelievable clarification from interviewer? (1,3,3)

annotation.definitionNote: 'I ask you!' is an exclamation meaning 'that's unbelievable', so the adjective stands for the whole cry

blocks.note: read as a cry of exasperated disbelief, the kind of exclamation that greets a tall story
taken literally, the interviewer pointing out who puts the questions

annotation.surface: An interviewer making an incredible statement to clear something up.
annotation.walkthrough: The question mark flags the literal second reading, which nobody would actually say.
annotation.definitionFit: Idiom: 'I ask you!' expresses disbelief; read literally, it is what an interviewer does.

entries.clue: Scholar startled with a gap regarding Egyptian tombs? (11)

indicatorNotes.startled: startled things jump about, so the letters are disturbed

annotation.surface: An Egyptologist shocked to find a gap in the tomb records.
annotation.walkthrough: The question mark admits the definition is by example: sarcophagi are not only Egyptian.
annotation.definitionFit: Sarcophagal means relating to a sarcophagus, the stone coffin found in Egyptian tombs.

entries.clue: Wind-player debuts in orchestra — Beethoven or Elgar? (4)

indicatorNotes.debuts in: the first appearance of each word, so its opening letter

blocks.note: first letters of Orchestra Beethoven Or Elgar

annotation.surface: A wind player making a first appearance with an orchestra, playing Beethoven or Elgar.
annotation.walkthrough: Wind-player looks like a person, but here the instrument itself is the player.
annotation.definitionFit: The oboe is a woodwind instrument, one that plays with wind.

entries.clue: Stick in garland with sense of certain vegetables (10)

indicatorNotes.in: the stick goes inside the garland

blocks.note: a lei is a Hawaiian garland

annotation.surface: Putting a stick in a flower garland that smells of vegetables.
annotation.walkthrough: Nous is everyday British for practical sense.
annotation.definitionFit: Leguminous means relating to legumes: peas, beans and lentils.

entries.clue: Working on teeth reduced conventional nervous response after end of operation (11)

indicatorNotes.reduced: conventional word loses its last letter
indicatorNotes.after: the twitch comes after the last letter of operation
indicatorNotes.end of: take the last letter of operation

blocks.note: a tic is a nervous twitch

annotation.surface: A dental patient twitching nervously after surgery.
annotation.walkthrough: Operation fits the dental surface, but only its last letter is used.
annotation.definitionFit: Orthodontics is the branch of dentistry that straightens teeth, so orthodontic work is working on teeth.

entries.clue: Trainer arranged opening of tennis courts in Rome at first (10)

indicatorNotes.arranged: the letters are put in a new order
indicatorNotes.at first: what comes at first in Rome is its opening letter

annotation.surface: A coach who organised the opening of tennis courts in Rome.
annotation.walkthrough: The Italian Open in Rome makes the tennis surface plausible; only T and R come from those words.
annotation.definitionFit: Plain synonym: a trainer instructs, whether in a gym or on a course.

entries.clue: Rough to lose a barge, dropping very lucky thing? (9)

indicatorNotes.to lose: the rough word goes without A
indicatorNotes.dropping: the barge word lets go of V

annotation.surface: A rough-edged boatman losing a barge while shedding a lucky charm.
annotation.walkthrough: Barge is a verb, to push, not a canal boat.
annotation.definitionFit: Definition by example: a horseshoe nailed over a door is a traditional good-luck charm.

entries.clue: Right number of degrees, say, I secure in New Year (6)

indicatorNotes.in: I and the secure word go inside New Year

blocks.note: to net is to secure, to catch

annotation.surface: Someone confirming the correct temperature, locked in over the New Year.
annotation.walkthrough: Right is a right angle, not correct; 'say' marks ninety as the example.
annotation.definitionFit: Geometry: a right angle measures ninety degrees, so ninety is the right angle's number.

entries.clue: Display of marching in triple time around a pair of rings (6)

indicatorNotes.around: the three times go around A

annotation.surface: A marching band keeping to three-four time around a couple of circles.
annotation.walkthrough: Triple time sounds musical, which suits marching; it just means three Ts.
annotation.definitionFit: Definition by example: a military tattoo, as at Edinburgh Castle, is a show of marching bands.

entries.clue: Artillery retaining one rule (9)

indicatorNotes.retaining: the artillery word keeps one inside

annotation.surface: A gun battery keeping to a single regulation.
annotation.walkthrough: Ordnance and ordinance differ by one letter, and that letter is the I.
annotation.definitionFit: Plain synonym, chiefly official: a local ordinance is a rule laid down by an authority.

entries.clue: Not going out (though agoraphobia isn’t the problem) (8)

annotation.definition: Not going out (though agoraphobia isn’t the problem)

blocks.note: the surface means staying at home; the setter means not going out like a light, not falling asleep
agoraphobia, fear of open or public places, is the obvious reason to stay in, and the aside rules it out

annotation.surface: Someone who stays in, though not from fear of open spaces.
annotation.walkthrough: The bracket pretends to help by ruling out a housebound reason, pushing the solver to look for another sense of going out.
annotation.definitionFit: Insomnia is the inability to sleep, to go out like a light.

entries.clue: Biblical character — I complain — is going West (5)

indicatorNotes.is going West: in an across clue, heading west means reading right to left

annotation.surface: A biblical figure grumbling about heading off west.
annotation.walkthrough: Going west can also mean dying or failing, but here it is direction only.
annotation.definitionFit: Definition by example: Naomi is Ruth's mother-in-law in the Book of Ruth.

entries.clue: Fashionable part of wedding dress is being prepared (2,5)

blocks.note: the train trails behind a wedding dress

annotation.surface: A trendy wedding dress with its train being got ready.
annotation.walkthrough: The wedding surface is apt: a train is what a bride has to get prepared.
annotation.definitionFit: A dated idiom: arrangements in train are under way, in the course of being prepared.

entries.clue: Pervade substance eaten by father overseas (8)

indicatorNotes.eaten by: the father word takes the substance inside it

blocks.note: the meat of an argument is its substance

annotation.surface: Something pervasive consumed by a father abroad.
annotation.walkthrough: Overseas means translate: père is the French father, and eaten suits MEAT going inside.
annotation.definitionFit: Plain synonym: a smell that permeates a room spreads right through it.

entries.clue: Italian dish, very dry, served in Brazilian city (7)

indicatorNotes.served in: the dish's pieces go inside the city, as food is served in a bowl

annotation.surface: A dry Italian dish on a menu in Rio.
annotation.walkthrough: Dry is of drink, not food: TT means teetotal.
annotation.definitionFit: Definition by example: risotto, rice cooked slowly in stock, comes from northern Italy.

entries.clue: Single line about King in the archives (2,6)

indicatorNotes.about: the single word goes around the King

blocks.note: a cord is a line, a string

annotation.surface: One line in the archives about a king.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Single line' looks like one phrase; the container splits it, putting R inside ONE only.
annotation.definitionFit: Idiom: what is on record has been written down and kept, as papers are in archives.

entries.clue: Female named after star dances topless and upside down (6)

indicatorNotes.topless: the dances word loses its first letter
indicatorNotes.upside down: in a down clue, the rest is read bottom to top

annotation.surface: A woman named after a celebrity dancing topless and upside down.
annotation.walkthrough: Star is a heavenly body, not a celebrity.
annotation.definitionFit: Stella is a woman's name taken from the Latin for star.

entries.clue: Economic statement showing the gravity of the situation? (4,4,2,4,4,4)

annotation.answer: WHAT GOES UP MUST COME DOWN
annotation.definition: Economic statement showing the gravity of the situation?

blocks.note: the surface suggests a budget speech; the setter means an economical, pithy saying, often applied to prices

blocks.clueFragment: showing the gravity of the situation?
blocks.note: gravity is not seriousness but the physical force that brings things back down

annotation.surface: An economist's warning about how serious things have become.
annotation.walkthrough: Gravity is both seriousness and the force: the proverb is a law of physics and a warning about booming prices.
annotation.definitionFit: The proverb states gravity's effect in eight words and is quoted of markets that have risen too far.

entries.clue: Run surplus? (5)

blocks.note: in cricket, a run not scored off the bat, such as a wide or a bye
surplus as an adjective, more than is needed, as in spare

annotation.walkthrough: Cricket's extras are runs added to the score without the batsman hitting the ball.

entries.clue: Line penned by comedian is flop (4)

indicatorNotes.penned by: the line is shut in by the comedian, as in a pen

blocks.note: a wit is a funny person

annotation.surface: A comedian's line that falls flat.

annotation.definitionFit: A verb sense: flowers that flop in the heat droop, which is to wilt.

entries.clue: I note jar, but I won’t be leaving tips (7)

blocks.note: the first I in the clue, as printed
n = note, as in footnote references
to jar on someone is to grate

annotation.surface: A diner who spots the tip jar and walks past it.
annotation.walkthrough: The tip jar in the surface is a decoy: jar is the verb, and the definition is the ungrateful customer's own words.

entries.clue: Hard time on encompassing most of the sporting event (9)

indicatorNotes.encompassing: the hard time goes around the rest
indicatorNotes.most of: drop the last letter of the

annotation.surface: An athlete struggling through most of a big race.
annotation.walkthrough: Hard time fits the gruelling race, but it just means an ordeal, a trial.
annotation.definitionFit: Definition by example: the triathlon is a race combining swimming, cycling and running.

entries.clue: Major figure ready to receive cheers (5)

indicatorNotes.to receive: the money word takes in the thanks

blocks.note: ready and tin are both old slang for cash

annotation.surface: A celebrity waiting to be applauded.
annotation.walkthrough: Ready means money (the readies), and cheers is British for thanks.
annotation.definitionFit: From the giants of Greek myth: a titan of industry is a major figure in it.

entries.clue: One hunting the good stories about National Trust craftsperson (6,7)

indicatorNotes.about: the stories go around the National Trust

blocks.note: NT = National Trust, the British heritage charity

annotation.surface: A heritage-charity potter who collects good stories.
annotation.walkthrough: The good is a noun here, the gifted ones, which is why it can stand alone.
annotation.definitionFit: A talent spotter searches for people who are good at something.

entries.clue: Area with new church in valley following a natural disaster (9)

indicatorNotes.in: area, new and church go inside valley
indicatorNotes.following: to follow is to come behind, so the valley pieces come behind a

annotation.surface: A valley church rebuilt after a landslide or snowslide.
annotation.walkthrough: The a that ends the clue belongs to the wordplay, not to 'a natural disaster'.
annotation.definitionFit: Definition by example: an avalanche is a sudden slide of snow down a mountain.
